Amami Oshima Island is one of Japan's Satsunan Islands (Kagoshima Prefecture). Being the largest within the Amami archipelago, the island covers a total area of approx 712 km2 (275 mi2) and has a population of around 73,000.

Administratively, the island is divided into Amami city, the towns of Tatsugo, Setouchi, and the villages Yamato and Uken. Much of the island is within Amami Gunto Quasi-National Park.

Amami Oshima is Japan's 7th largest island in the Japanese archipelago, excluding the disputed Kuril Islands. It is approx 380 km (210 mi) south of the southern tip of Kyushu Island and approx 250 km (130 mi) north of Okinawa.

The island's highest elevation point (Mount Yuwanda) is 605 m (1985 ft) above sea level. The coast is surrounded by a coral reef. The Pacific Ocean is on the east and the East China Sea - on the west.

The climate is humid subtropical, with mild winters and very warm summers. The rainy season is May through September. The island is subject to repeated typhoons.

The island's economy is based mainly on agriculture (rice, sweet potatoes, sugarcane), commercial fishing, the distillation of shochu (an alcoholic beverage with 45% alcohol by volume), and seasonal tourism. The favorable climate allows for 2 rice crops per year. Traditional crafts include hand-made silk.

Amami City's Port Naze is a major regional ferry port. The island is also served by Amami Airport (on the northern end) linking it via domestic flights with Tokyo, Naha, Fukuoka, Kagoshima and Osaka, and via short flights to other Amami islands.

Since March 2018, Amami-Oshima is connected to the Yakushima islands via a weekly cruise ferry service. The charter flight service between the islands was started in February 2018. Amami-Oshima tourism was also boosted by the introduction of new routes connecting sightseeing sites in Kagoshima Prefecture. Until 2018, there were no ferries or flights directly linking the islands.

The ferry service's 1-year trial started on March 4, 2018. The regularly scheduled service is offered once every 4 days. It links Naha with Kagoshima via Port Naze (Amami-Oshima Island). The cruise ferry also visits Port Miyanoura (Yakushima Island) if at least 20 passengers make reservations.

Amami Oshima Island Japan cruise terminal

Cruise ships to Amami Oshima Island dock (anchor) at Amami (Port Naze) - a port town located on the northern coast.

At a Glance

Independent with some planning or transport. Central Naze is close enough for an easy independent visit, but Amami Oshima’s mangroves, beaches and protected forests are spread across a large island. Taxis, a pre-arranged driver or an organized excursion are more practical than relying on infrequent buses for the main nature sights.

Getting from Naze Cruise Port

Ships generally call at Naze Port on the northwestern side of Amami Oshima. The Nagahama area has a dedicated cruise berth, although the exact arrival arrangement can depend on the ship and local operations. Check the onboard notice to confirm whether your sailing will dock or use tenders.

  • On foot: From the Nagahama cruise berth, the center of Naze is roughly a 15–20-minute walk. The route is mostly level and leads to shops, restaurants and the central shopping streets.
  • Taxi: The most useful option for beaches and attractions outside town. Availability may be limited when a ship is visiting, so advance arrangements are sensible for a longer island tour.
  • Local bus: Shima Bus connects Naze with other parts of the island, including the Mangrove Park corridor. Services outside the principal routes are limited, and waiting for the return bus can consume a significant part of a port call.
  • Shuttle: Any cruise-line or local shuttle arrangement varies by sailing and should be confirmed onboard.

Best Ways to Spend the Call

Mangrove Canoeing

The mangrove forest at Kuroshio no Mori Mangrove Park is one of the island’s signature experiences. It is approximately 30–40 minutes by road from central Naze, with organized canoe sessions generally lasting about one hour.

Allow approximately 3–4 hours for transfers, check-in and paddling. A pre-booked excursion or private transfer is preferable because canoe departures are scheduled and public buses may not fit the ship’s timetable. Conditions in the channels vary with the tide.

Naze Town and Amami Culture

For a flexible day without a long transfer, explore Naze independently. The Amami City Amami Museum in Nagahama introduces the island’s natural environment, history and traditional life. Continue into the commercial center for local food, shops and examples of Oshima Tsumugi silk textiles.

This option needs approximately 2–3 hours and is the safest choice for a short call, uncertain weather or passengers who prefer to remain close to the ship.

Ohama Seaside Park

Ohama Seaside Park combines a coral-sand beach, coastal views, a promenade and the Amami Ocean Exhibition Hall. It is approximately 15–20 minutes by taxi from central Naze.

Allow 2–3 hours including transport. Swimming should depend on weather, sea conditions and any local warnings; the beach is also worthwhile simply for a coastal walk. Arrange the return taxi rather than assuming one will be waiting.

Kinsakubaru Forest

Kinsakubaru protects subtropical old-growth forest and endemic wildlife. Entry is permitted only with a certified eco-tour guide, reservations are required, and vehicle numbers are controlled. The forest route is approximately 2 km (1.2 mi), generally taking 1.5–2 hours on foot.

Organized excursion recommended. Access involves narrow mountain roads, and there is no reliable mobile-phone signal in parts of the area. Allow at least half a day including transfers.

Island Highlights by Car

A private driver or organized tour can combine one principal nature experience with a beach, viewpoint or textile-related stop. Avoid attempting both the far north and far south during an ordinary port call: the island is long, roads are often winding, and transfers take longer than distances may suggest.

Self-Guided Naze Walking Tour

Easy Town and Culture Route

Route: Nagahama cruise berth – Amami City Amami Museum – Nagahama waterfront – central shopping streets – Yanigawa entertainment district – return to the port.

  1. Begin at the passenger exit and walk through Nagahama to the Amami City Amami Museum.
  2. Allow time for the exhibits if the museum is open during the call.
  3. Continue toward central Naze and its covered and open-air shopping streets.
  4. Walk through the Yanigawa area, known locally for its compact lanes of restaurants and small bars.
  5. Stop for an Amami-style meal or browse for local silk goods before retracing the route to the ship.

The complete circuit is approximately 4 km (2.5 mi), with about 50–60 minutes of pure walking. Allow 2–3 hours with museum, shopping and refreshment stops. The route is mostly flat and easy, although summer heat, humidity and heavy rain can make it tiring.

Practical Tips

  • Reserve mangrove canoeing, forest guiding and private transport before arrival whenever possible.
  • Carry some Japanese yen; smaller taxis, shops and local businesses may not accept every foreign card.
  • English may be limited outside organized tourism services. Keep the port name or berth location available in Japanese for the return journey.
  • Wear sun protection and carry water. Amami Oshima can be hot, humid and wet, with sudden showers.
  • For attractions outside Naze, plan to be back at the port at least 60–90 minutes before the required all-aboard time. Allow additional time when tendering or using a scheduled public bus.
